name: Burial of the dead
desc: The band buries its dead with ochre and ornaments and mourns them together, binding the living to one another and to the places where their kin lie.
distinctFrom: shamanic_ritual is a specialist's role; burial is a community-wide rite needing no specialist. ancestor_veneration (A2) is the later settled cult of named ancestors.

name: Sacred gathering places
desc: Bands that live apart meet at painted caves and shrines in certain seasons to hold rites, exchange news and find spouses.
distinctFrom: shamanic_ritual is who leads the rite; this is where scattered bands gather for it.

name: Prestige leadership
desc: Some men and women lead by skill and generosity rather than birth: others follow them on the hunt, in moves and in disputes, but can leave them at will.
distinctFrom: kin_council is collective deliberation; this is personal, achieved authority within it. hereditary_rank (A2) is authority by birth.

name: Monumental shrines
desc: Communities raise stone enclosures and tombs too large for any household, feeding the work parties with feasts and gathering at them for rites.
distinctFrom: communal_feasts is the feast; this is the monument the feast pays for. corvee_labour (A3) is labour owed to a state, not volunteered to a shrine.

name: Insignia of rank
desc: Sceptres, maces and gold ornaments mark who holds rank, so authority is recognized by people who have never met its holder.
distinctFrom: hereditary_rank is the rule of inheritance; regalia are its visible signs, which carry authority beyond face-to-face contact.

name: First-comer precedence
desc: The lineage descended from the first settlers keeps the shrine of the land and allots fields to later arrivals, who farm by its leave.
distinctFrom: ancestor_veneration honours the dead; this turns descent from the first settlers into a claim over land and newcomers.

name: Segmentary lineage society
desc: Lineages unite against outsiders and split when they grow, with no permanent chief; elders of each segment settle disputes.
distinctFrom: chiefdom has a permanent paramount; tribal_confederacy is a sworn league. This form has neither: unity by descent, fission by growth.

name: Big-man polity
desc: Leaders compete for followers by sponsoring feasts and exchanges; their authority lasts only as long as their generosity and is not inherited.
distinctFrom: chiefdom is hereditary office; the big-man's position is achieved and lapses with him.

name: Enthronement rites
desc: A new ruler is installed by public rite: anointing, crowning and the oath of the great men, so everyone knows who rules from the day of accession.
distinctFrom: succession_law says who the heir is; this rite makes the accession public and binding.

name: State pantheon
desc: The city gods are arranged in one ranked family under a high god, whose shrine confers kingship over all the cities.
distinctFrom: organized_priesthood serves one city's god; this joins many cities' gods into one hierarchy that legitimizes rule over all of them.

name: Temple relief
desc: Temples put widows, orphans and the destitute on their ration lists in return for light work, so the weakest are fed from temple stores.
distinctFrom: temple_economy is the estate management; this is the temple's relief role. debt_remission is a royal edict cancelling debts.

name: Overkingship
desc: A great king rules other kings, who keep their thrones in return for oaths, tribute and troops.
distinctFrom: territorial_kingship rules directly through officials; overkingship rules indirectly through sworn sub-kings.

name: Succession oaths
desc: Officials and vassal kings swear in the old ruler's lifetime to support his chosen heir, under curses if they break the oath.
distinctFrom: succession_law names the heir; these oaths bind the realm's officials to him before the accession.

name: Ethical religion
desc: Prophets teach that the gods demand justice for the poor rather than sacrifice alone, and judge kings and the rich by that standard.
distinctFrom: organized_priesthood is the cult; this is the moral content that holds rulers and rich to account. scriptural_canon fixes texts.

name: Pilgrimage and sacred truce
desc: Sanctuaries draw pilgrims from many states; a sacred truce protects travellers on the roads to the festival.
distinctFrom: public_games is the contest; pilgrimage is the protected journey and the sanctuary network.

name: Tyranny
desc: A strongman seizes a city outside the traditional order, backed by the people or hired troops, and rules through patronage and public works.
distinctFrom: military_rule is government by the armed forces as a body; tyranny is one man's rule over a city, outside law but often popular.

name: Ruler cult
desc: Provinces raise temples and priests to the living or deified ruler; local notables compete to hold the priesthood, binding them to the empire.
distinctFrom: sacral_kingship is the king's sanction by the gods; the ruler cult makes him an object of provincial worship run by local elites.

name: Adoptive succession
desc: The ruler adopts the ablest candidate as his son and heir, giving merit the form of dynastic succession.
distinctFrom: succession_law fixes the heir by birth order; adoption chooses him by ability while keeping dynastic form.

name: Congregations
desc: Lay believers meet weekly to hear scripture, share a meal and support their poor, sick and widows from a common fund.
distinctFrom: organized_priesthood and temple_almsgiving are run by priests; congregations are lay communities supporting their own members.

name: State orthodoxy
desc: One school of thought is made the state's official doctrine: its classics are taught at a state academy and mastery of them leads to office.
distinctFrom: state_religion establishes a faith and clergy; state orthodoxy establishes a doctrine and a curriculum for officials.

name: Pious endowments
desc: Land and shops are endowed in perpetuity to fund hospitals, fountains, schools and kitchens, managed by trustees under religious law.
distinctFrom: temple_almsgiving is relief from temple stores; endowments are perpetual legal trusts with their own income.

name: Church-state concordat
desc: Church and crown divide authority over bishops: the church confers spiritual office, the ruler the lands, ending wars over who appoints them.
distinctFrom: state_religion makes the church official; the concordat sets the boundary between church and crown.

name: Mendicant friars
desc: Friars without property preach and beg in the towns, nursing the sick and serving the urban poor.
distinctFrom: monasticism withdraws from the world to estates; friars live among townspeople without estates.

name: Holy war
desc: War against unbelievers is declared a religious duty with spiritual rewards, and conquered frontier land is settled by the faithful.
distinctFrom: military_orders are the fighting monks; this is the doctrine that sanctions the war and the settlement behind it.

name: Primogeniture
desc: The eldest son inherits the realm or fief undivided; younger sons go to the church, the army or abroad.
distinctFrom: succession_law names an heir; primogeniture also keeps the inheritance undivided.

name: Caliphate
desc: The successor of the Prophet leads the community of believers in war, law and taxation, through governors and a register of revenues.
distinctFrom: theocracy is rule by priests under religious law; the caliph is a lay successor-ruler, not a priest.

name: Confessional state
desc: Each ruler fixes his territory's confession; the church keeps parish registers of births, marriages and deaths and disciplines the parish.
distinctFrom: state_religion establishes a faith; confessionalization builds parish registration and discipline in each territory's confession.

name: Revival movements
desc: Lay devotional circles call for personal conversion and good works, founding orphanages, charity schools and Bible societies.
distinctFrom: religious_reform founds new churches; revivalism renews piety inside them and builds charitable foundations.

name: Reason of state
desc: The interest of the state is placed above religious and dynastic claims: rulers build revenue, armies and alliances for the state's sake.
distinctFrom: statecraft_doctrine is advice to rulers; reason of state elevates the state's interest above faith and dynasty.

name: Plebiscitary legitimacy
desc: A ruler seeks the people's direct approval in a yes-or-no vote on his rule or constitution, bypassing representatives.
distinctFrom: referendum lets citizens decide a law; a plebiscite asks them to endorse a ruler or regime.

name: Civic ritual
desc: Flags, anthems, national holidays and monuments give the sovereign nation its own rites, celebrated in every town.
distinctFrom: nationalism is the doctrine; civic ritual is its calendar of festivals and symbols.

name: Social Christianity
desc: Churches take up the labour question, backing fair wages, workers' associations, settlement houses and relief for the industrial poor.
distinctFrom: socialism demands collective ownership; social Christianity seeks reform within property and church.

name: Missionary societies
desc: Voluntary societies fund missionaries abroad, who found schools and clinics and send home reports and maps of the interior.
distinctFrom: missionary_religion is the duty to convert; these are the organized, subscription-funded overseas societies.

name: Plebiscitary empire
desc: An emperor rules with authoritarian powers confirmed by plebiscites, through prefects, a mass army and public works.
distinctFrom: absolute_monarchy rests on dynastic right; this form rests on plebiscites and the mass army.

name: Feminism
desc: A movement claims for women the rights of citizens: education, property, the professions and the vote.
distinctFrom: womens_suffrage is the vote; feminism is the wider movement for education, property and work.

name: Social democracy
desc: Socialist parties seek reform through elections and parliament: social insurance, labour law and public services instead of revolution.
distinctFrom: socialism is the movement's goal; social democracy is its parliamentary, reformist strategy.

name: New imperialism
desc: Overseas empire is argued to be a national necessity and a civilizing mission; colonies are claimed and settled by agreement among powers.
distinctFrom: colonial_administration governs colonies; this is the doctrine that drives their acquisition.

name: Progressivism
desc: Reformers use investigative journalism, experts and regulation to clean up cities, food, factories and politics.
distinctFrom: classical_liberalism limits government; progressivism uses it to regulate.

name: Semi-presidential republic
desc: A directly elected president shares executive power with a prime minister responsible to parliament.
distinctFrom: presidential_republic has no prime minister responsible to parliament; parliamentary_government has no elected president with real powers.

name: Dominant-party system
desc: One party wins every election for decades while opposition parties remain legal; politics happens among its factions.
distinctFrom: one_party_state bans other parties; here opposition is legal but never wins.

name: Personalist dictatorship
desc: One man rules through family, cronies and a loyal guard, above any party or army institution.
distinctFrom: military_rule is rule by the army as a body; one_party_state by a party; here power is personal.

name: Clerical republic
desc: Elected institutions govern under the guardianship of senior clerics, who can veto laws and candidates.
distinctFrom: theocracy is government by religious office; here elected republican institutions sit under clerical guardianship.

name: Supranational union
desc: Member states pool sovereignty in common institutions with their own law, court and market, and allow free movement of goods and people.
distinctFrom: federal_republic is one sovereign state; a supranational union pools only part of its members' sovereignty.

name: Cult of personality
desc: The leader is glorified as infallible in portraits, songs and slogans; loyalty to him becomes the test of loyalty to the state.
distinctFrom: state_propaganda is a ministry and method; the cult concentrates legitimacy in one person.

name: Constitutional court
desc: A special court rules on whether laws and official acts are constitutional and settles disputes between branches and levels of government.
distinctFrom: judicial_review is any court's power to void laws; this is a dedicated court that arbitrates the constitution itself.

name: Transitional justice
desc: After a dictatorship or civil war, truth commissions, trials and reparations establish what happened and give the new order legitimacy.
distinctFrom: international_tribunals try individuals; transitional justice is the domestic process that legitimizes a new regime.

name: Power-sharing
desc: Offices, seats and vetoes are divided among a country's communities by agreement, so no group can rule the others alone.
distinctFrom: federal_republic divides power by territory; power-sharing divides it among communities.

name: Term limits
desc: The head of government may serve only a fixed number of terms, forcing regular turnover at the top.
distinctFrom: presidential_republic fixes terms; term limits cap how many a person may hold.

name: Independent electoral administration
desc: Elections are run by an independent body of officials, not by the government in power, so results are trusted by losers.
distinctFrom: secret_ballot protects the voter; this protects the count and the electoral roll.

name: Ceremonial monarchy
desc: The hereditary monarch keeps only ceremonial duties as a non-partisan symbol of the state, above party politics.
distinctFrom: constitutional_monarchy still gives the monarch political powers; here the role is purely symbolic.

name: Ecumenical movement
desc: Churches and faiths cooperate through councils and dialogue instead of competing for converts and condemning one another.
distinctFrom: religious_toleration is state policy; ecumenism is cooperation among the faiths themselves.

name: Liberation theology
desc: Clergy and lay base communities read scripture as a call to free the poor, organizing cooperatives, soup kitchens and land claims.
distinctFrom: social_christianity is reform from above; liberation theology organizes the poor themselves.

name: Religious mass movements
desc: Mass movements seek to order state and society by religious values, combining preaching, welfare networks and electoral politics.
distinctFrom: state_religion is establishment by a ruler; these are mass movements from below.

name: Religious relief agencies
desc: Religious agencies run famine relief, child feeding and refugee aid across borders.
distinctFrom: temple_almsgiving is local; these are international agencies with supply chains.

name: Vanguard party
desc: A disciplined party of professional revolutionaries claims to lead the working class, seize power and run the state in its name.
distinctFrom: socialism is the movement; the vanguard party is its Leninist organization for taking power.

name: Nonviolent resistance
desc: Movements break unjust laws openly and without violence, using boycotts, strikes and marches to win public opinion.
distinctFrom: civil_rights_law is the legal result; nonviolent resistance is the method that won it.

name: Neoliberalism
desc: Markets are promoted over state management: privatization, deregulation, independent central banks and open capital flows.
distinctFrom: classical_liberalism argued against mercantilism; neoliberalism against the post-war mixed economy.

name: Developmental state
desc: The state guides private industry with credit, targets and protection to catch up with industrial nations.
distinctFrom: central_planning replaces markets; the developmental state steers private firms within them.

name: Multiculturalism
desc: The state recognizes and supports the cultures of immigrant and minority communities as part of the nation.
distinctFrom: secular_state treats faiths equally; multiculturalism supports distinct communities' cultures.

name: Environmentalism
desc: A mass movement demands protection of air, water, land and climate, and green parties enter parliaments.
distinctFrom: environmental_regulation is the law; environmentalism is the movement that demands it.

name: Mass populism
desc: A leader claims to speak for the common people against the elite, winning elections and bringing unions under the state.
distinctFrom: fascism abolishes elections; populism wins them and keeps them.

name: Modernizing nationalism
desc: A nationalist state modernizes by decree: secular law, script reform, Western dress and mass schooling.
distinctFrom: nationalism defines the nation; this programme remakes its society from above.

name: Social liberalism
desc: Liberals accept that the state must insure citizens against unemployment, sickness and old age to keep a free society.
distinctFrom: classical_liberalism limits the state; social liberalism adds social insurance.

name: Liberal internationalism
desc: Peace is to be kept by open trade, self-determination and international institutions.
distinctFrom: collective_security is the alliance mechanism; liberal internationalism is the doctrine behind it.

name: Pan-national movements
desc: Movements unite peoples across many states by shared language, history or continent, and found regional organizations.
distinctFrom: nationalism builds one nation-state; pan-national movements unite many.

name: Customary sanctions
desc: Ridicule, shunning and, at the last, expulsion from the band keep bullies and shirkers in line. Everyone knows the rules because everyone tells them.
distinctFrom: kin_council decides matters at a meeting; customary sanctions are the band's standing penalties applied without one.

name: Band territories
desc: Each band holds a known range. In a lean season its members may forage on a neighbour's land by asking leave through kin and exchange partners.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange moves objects between partners; band territories govern who may use which land and how access is asked.

name: Seasonal gatherings
desc: Several bands meet at a rich place each year to feast, trade, arrange marriages and settle quarrels between groups, then disperse again.
distinctFrom: kin_council governs one band; seasonal gatherings bring many bands together for a few weeks.

name: Compensation for injury
desc: A killing or injury is settled by a fixed payment from the offender's kin to the victim's, set by the elders, instead of by revenge.
distinctFrom: customary_sanctions punish a band member; compensation settles wrongs between kin groups by payment.

name: Witnessed agreements
desc: A sale, loan or pledge is made before named witnesses who can later swear to its terms, so a deal with a stranger can be enforced.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange is reciprocity between partners; witnessed agreements bind strangers to stated terms.

name: Household fields
desc: Each household works its own fields within marked boundaries and passes them to its heirs; the village recognizes the holding.
distinctFrom: C1's first_settler_rights lets a founding lineage allot fields; household fields are heritable holdings of each household.

name: Sealed stores
desc: Store doors and jars are closed with clay pressed by an owner's seal; a broken sealing shows who took grain and when.
distinctFrom: stamp_seal is the object; sealed stores are the custom of controlling and auditing store access with it.

name: Village headship
desc: One household head is acknowledged as the village's head: he speaks for it to outsiders and calls the households to common work.
distinctFrom: kin_council decides by consensus; headship is a standing office in a settled village, not a regional chief (C1 chiefdom).

name: Judges and court records
desc: Appointed judges hear cases, take witnesses' oaths and record the verdict on a tablet, so a decided case stays decided.
distinctFrom: law_code is the text of the law; royal judges are the office that applies it and keeps records of verdicts.

name: Ration lists
desc: Dependents of temple and palace draw fixed monthly rations of barley, oil and wool by age and status, so a short year is shared out by rule.
distinctFrom: temple_economy is the institution; ration lists are the written scale by which its stores are paid out.

name: Village and ward heads
desc: A head chosen in the village or city ward answers to the palace for its dues, labour levies and crimes, and speaks for it before officials.
distinctFrom: elite_council is a council of great families at the centre; village heads link each local community to the state.

name: Merchant colony courts
desc: Merchants abroad form a colony with its own court; disputes over debts and lost goods are settled on the spot under the home city's law.
distinctFrom: C3's commercial_law (A6) is a general merchant law; karum courts are an early colony court abroad.

name: Published laws
desc: Laws are carved on stone and set up in public so any citizen who can read knows the rule and the penalty, and magistrates cannot invent them.
distinctFrom: law_code is law written by and for officials; published law is displayed for citizens to read.

name: Royal storehouses
desc: Revenue in grain, wine and silver is held in sealed provincial storehouses and paid out only by written order, keeping years of reserves.
distinctFrom: storehouse_sealing controls one store; the treasury is a provincial network of stores run on written orders.

name: Property classes
desc: Citizens are ranked by assessed wealth instead of birth; a family that grows rich can climb into the classes that may hold office.
distinctFrom: elite_council admits leading families by birth; property classes admit by assessed wealth.

name: Extended citizenship
desc: Citizenship is granted to allies, freedmen and whole towns; new citizens may marry, trade, sue and settle anywhere under the common law.
distinctFrom: citizen_assembly is the body of citizens; extended citizenship opens it to outsiders by law.

name: Selection by lot
desc: Many offices are filled by drawing lots among eligible citizens, so no faction can buy or monopolize them and every citizen may serve.
distinctFrom: elected_magistracies choose by vote; sortition by lot.

name: Household registers
desc: Every household is entered on a standing register kept by county officials, updated for births, deaths and moves; groups of five answer for each other's dues.
distinctFrom: census is a periodic count; household registers are continuous and tie each household to duties.

name: Courts of appeal
desc: A higher court reviews the judgments of local judges and petitions against officials; a wrong verdict can be overturned without bribing the governor.
distinctFrom: royal_judges decide cases at first instance; appellate courts review those decisions.

name: Public notaries
desc: Licensed notaries draw up contracts, wills and sales in set forms and keep registers; a notarial deed is proof in any court.
distinctFrom: witnessed_agreements rely on living witnesses; a notarial deed is a public record that proves itself.

name: Law faculties
desc: Masters lecture on the Roman Digest and train students in glossing and disputation; their graduates staff courts and chanceries across the realm.
distinctFrom: jurists are practitioners; law faculties are the organized teaching of law in universities.

name: Exchequer audit
desc: Sheriffs account twice a year at a chequered counting table; sums owed and paid are written on rolls, and arrears follow the official until cleared.
distinctFrom: taxation declares the levy; the Exchequer audits each collector's account against it.

name: Chancery enrolment
desc: Copies of every letter and writ sent out are entered on rolls, so the government knows what it has granted and ordered and can enforce it.
distinctFrom: royal_archives keep incoming records; chancery rolls copy every outgoing order.

name: Village by-laws
desc: The village meeting sets the dates of ploughing, harvest and gleaning and the number of beasts on the common, and fines those who break the rules.
distinctFrom: municipal_charter governs towns; village by-laws govern open-field farming by the village meeting.

name: Intendants
desc: Royal commissioners, removable at will and paid by the crown, oversee justice, police and finance in each province and report by post to the council.
distinctFrom: provincial_administration places governors; intendants are revocable commissioners checking them and the venal officers.

name: Bankruptcy law
desc: When a trader fails, his goods are gathered and shared among creditors by rule, and an honest debtor can be discharged and trade again.
distinctFrom: commercial_law covers contracts between solvent merchants; bankruptcy law governs what happens when one fails.

name: Administrative courts
desc: Citizens can sue the administration before specialist judges; officials who exceed their powers see their acts annulled, so every province is run by the same rules.
distinctFrom: judicial_review tests laws against the constitution; administrative courts test officials' acts against the law.

name: Penitentiaries
desc: Prison terms graded by offence replace branding, flogging and the gallows for most crimes; convicts are held, worked and released rather than maimed or killed.
distinctFrom: civil_police arrests offenders; penitentiaries decide what is done with them after conviction.

name: Married women's property
desc: A wife keeps her own earnings, property and inheritance and may contract and sue in her own name, so women can run shops and enter trades.
distinctFrom: family_law fixes marriage and inheritance; this act gives wives separate legal personality in property.

name: Trademark law
desc: Makers register their marks and copying one is a wrong, so buyers far away can trust a branded sack of flour or tin of tea.
distinctFrom: patent protects an invention; a trademark protects a maker's name on goods.

name: Prefects
desc: Each uniform department is run by a prefect appointed by and answering to the interior ministry, applying the same laws, levies and conscription everywhere.
distinctFrom: provincial_intendants supervised historic provinces with mixed privileges; prefects run uniform departments under one ministry.

name: Civil registration
desc: Every birth, marriage and death is recorded by a public registrar; each person has a legal identity, and the state sees where infants are dying.
distinctFrom: official_statistics publishes tables; civil registration is the record of each person from which they are drawn.

name: Abolition of internal tolls
desc: Tolls at provincial borders, rivers and town gates are abolished; duties are collected once, at the national frontier, by one customs service.
distinctFrom: customs_tolls levy duties at internal gates; this replaces them with one frontier tariff. C3's customs_union joins several states' tariffs.

name: Elected town councils
desc: Ratepayers elect a town council with a budget of its own; it paves, lights and drains streets and maintains the roads of its district.
distinctFrom: municipal_charter grants self-government to an oligarchy; elected councils answer to all ratepayers and run public works.

name: Elected rural councils
desc: Elected district councils of landowners, townsmen and peasants run rural schools, clinics, roads and grain reserves for relief in bad years.
distinctFrom: municipal_corporations govern towns; zemstvos govern the countryside.

name: Patent Cooperation Treaty
desc: One international application and search covers many countries: inventors file once, and laboratories can see what is already claimed anywhere.
distinctFrom: patent is a national grant; this is one international filing and search for all members.

name: Land to the tiller
desc: The state buys out absentee landlords and sells their land in small plots to the tenants who farm it; owner-farmers invest in their own fields.
distinctFrom: household_land_tenure recognizes existing holdings; land reform transfers land from landlords to tenants.

name: Tenancy protection
desc: Sharecroppers are registered and cannot be evicted while they pay a fixed share; secure tenants manure, drain and double-crop the land.
distinctFrom: land_reform transfers ownership; tenancy protection leaves ownership but secures the tenant.

name: International arbitration
desc: Traders in different countries choose private arbitrators whose awards courts everywhere enforce, so a cross-border deal no longer hangs on a foreign judge.
distinctFrom: karum_courts settled disputes within one merchant colony; arbitration awards are enforceable across states.

name: Refugee protection
desc: People fleeing persecution receive travel papers and may not be sent back to danger; states share the task of receiving them.
distinctFrom: human_rights declares rights in general; refugee law gives a specific status and travel papers to the displaced.

name: Equal pay law
desc: Employers must pay women the same as men for the same work, so more women train for and stay in skilled and professional jobs.
distinctFrom: married_womens_property gave wives control of earnings; equal pay governs what employers must pay.

name: Consumer protection
desc: Labels must state contents, weights must be true and dangerous goods can be recalled, so buyers trust goods from distant makers.
distinctFrom: trademark_law protects the seller's mark; consumer protection protects the buyer against the seller.

name: Legal aid
desc: The state pays for a lawyer for those who cannot afford one, in criminal trials and in disputes over wages, housing and family.
distinctFrom: jurists serve those who can pay; legal aid extends counsel to everyone.

name: Tax withholding
desc: Employers deduct income tax from every wage packet and pay it to the state; wage earners pay as they earn and evasion falls.
distinctFrom: income_tax assesses declared incomes; withholding collects it at the payroll.

name: Value-added tax
desc: Each firm pays tax on the value it adds and deducts the tax paid on its inputs; invoices check one another, and exports leave untaxed.
distinctFrom: customs_tolls tax goods at gates; VAT taxes value added at each stage with credit for tax already paid.

name: Executive budget
desc: A central budget office prepares one plan of revenue and spending for every department and audits it afterwards, so distant agencies spend as planned.
distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks collectors after the fact; the executive budget plans all spending before it happens.

name: Sample surveys
desc: Statisticians measure a random sample of fields and households instead of all, giving crop and employment estimates within weeks, in time to move stocks.
distinctFrom: official_statistics counts everyone; sample surveys estimate quickly from a random part.

name: Fiscal equalization
desc: The central treasury transfers revenue to poorer or stricken regions by formula, so provinces can keep services and relief going after a bad year.
distinctFrom: income_tax raises revenue; equalization moves it to regions that need it.

name: Customs modernization
desc: Goods are classified by one world nomenclature and declared electronically; most cargo clears in hours, with checks targeted by risk.
distinctFrom: internal_toll_abolition removes internal duties; customs modernization speeds the frontier itself.

name: Competitive procurement
desc: Public works are let by open, advertised tender under published rules, and contracts go to the lowest compliant bid rather than to friends of officials.
distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks what was spent; procurement governs how contracts are awarded.

name: Agricultural extension
desc: Public agents trained at agricultural colleges visit farms, run demonstration plots and teach new seed, fertiliser and methods to working farmers.
distinctFrom: agricultural_chemistry is the science; extension is the public service that carries it to farmers.

name: Disaster management
desc: A standing agency plans for flood, drought and earthquake, stocks relief, broadcasts warnings and moves food and shelter to the stricken within days.
distinctFrom: zemstvo_councils kept local grain reserves; a disaster agency plans and moves relief nationally.

name: Freedom of information
desc: Any citizen may request government files and must receive them unless a stated exemption applies, so abuses come to light and are corrected.
distinctFrom: C5's press_freedom lets publishers print; freedom of information compels the state to open its files.

name: Digital government
desc: Citizens file taxes, register businesses and claim benefits online; agencies share data through secure links, so remote districts are served as well as the capital.
distinctFrom: chancery_rolls and executive_budget are paper records; digital government delivers the services themselves online.

name: Digital identity
desc: Every resident has a unique, verifiable digital identity; entitlements such as rations and pensions can be drawn anywhere, so workers can move without losing them.
distinctFrom: civil_registration records identity on paper locally; digital identity verifies it anywhere online.

name: Road traffic law
desc: Licensed drivers, registered vehicles, speed limits, uniform signs and right-of-way rules let heavy motor traffic flow safely between towns.
distinctFrom: C3's zoning plans land use; traffic law governs movement on the roads.

name: Anti-corruption commission
desc: An independent commission investigates officials' bribes and kickbacks with power to arrest, so revenue stops leaking between taxpayer and treasury.
distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks accounts; an anti-corruption commission investigates and prosecutes officials.

name: Administrative procedure law
desc: Agencies must publish proposed rules, hear comments and give reasons for decisions, which courts can review; those affected are heard before, not after.
distinctFrom: administrative_courts annul unlawful acts afterwards; administrative procedure governs how decisions are made.

name: Proportional representation
desc: Seats are shared among parties in proportion to their votes, so minorities and new movements win a voice in the chamber instead of the street.
distinctFrom: mass_suffrage gives everyone a vote; proportional representation makes each vote count toward seats.

name: Regional self-government
desc: Elected regional assemblies and governments take over schools, health and roads within a region, extending effective government to its far corners.
distinctFrom: provincial_administration appoints governors from the centre; devolution elects regional governments.

name: Reserved seats
desc: A share of seats and council headships is set aside for excluded castes, tribes or women; their members gain office, patronage and a route upward.
distinctFrom: C1's power_sharing divides offices among communities; reserved seats guarantee places for disadvantaged groups within any party system.

name: Participatory budgeting
desc: Neighbourhood assemblies vote each year on which streets, drains and clinics the city's investment budget will build, and monitor the works.
distinctFrom: municipal_corporations decide budgets in council; participatory budgeting gives the decision to neighbourhood assemblies.

name: Elected village councils
desc: Every village elects a council with its own funds and duties; it runs public works and relief schemes and decides who needs help when harvests fail.
distinctFrom: zemstvo_councils govern a district; elected village councils govern each village.

name: Metropolitan government
desc: One authority plans transport, water and land use for a city and its suburbs together, so the whole commuting region works as one.
distinctFrom: municipal_corporations govern within city limits; metropolitan government spans the whole urban region.

name: Food-sharing norms
desc: Whoever brings in meat must share it with the whole band. A hunter's bad week no longer starves his children, and no family hoards while others go hungry.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange moves goods between bands; food sharing divides food within the band.

name: Seasonal round
desc: The band moves between known camps on a fixed yearly schedule, reaching fish runs, nut groves and herds when each is at its best.
distinctFrom: transhumance (A2) moves herds between pastures; the seasonal round moves the whole band between wild resources.

name: Fire-stick land management
desc: The band burns country in small patches at chosen seasons, opening grassland that draws game and renews food plants.
distinctFrom: fire_making is the technique; this is the shared rule of when and where the band burns its land.

name: Communal storehouses
desc: The village keeps its grain in common storehouses under agreed rules, so a household with a poor crop can draw on the common stock.
distinctFrom: public_granaries (A5) is a state buffer stock sold in dearth; this is a village pool held in common.

name: Transhumance
desc: Herders move flocks between summer mountain pastures and winter lowlands along customary routes, so neither range is grazed bare.
distinctFrom: stinted_commons (A6) caps beasts on one common; transhumance moves herds between distant pastures.

name: Craft specialization
desc: Some households work part-time as potters, bead-makers or smiths and exchange their wares for food.
distinctFrom: craft_guilds (A5) regulates organised trades; this is the first appearance of specialists at all.

name: Barter of staples
desc: Villagers trade surplus grain, salt and stone with neighbours at agreed equivalents, without waiting for a gift to be returned.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange is reciprocal and delayed between partners; barter is an immediate exchange of equivalents.

name: Reciprocal work parties
desc: Households call on neighbours to raise houses and bring in harvests, repaying with food, drink and labour in turn.
distinctFrom: corvee_labour (A3) is labour owed to a ruler; work parties are reciprocal among equals.

name: Ration distribution
desc: Temple and palace issue standard monthly rations of barley, oil and wool to workers, widows and orphans on their lists.
distinctFrom: public_granaries (A5) sells and issues stock in dearth; rations are a routine, standing payment in kind.

name: Interest-bearing loans
desc: Temples and merchants lend barley and silver at fixed interest, recorded on sealed tablets, to finance seed and caravans.
distinctFrom: debt_remission cancels debts; this is the credit contract itself.

name: Wage and hire tariffs
desc: The law fixes what a harvester, an ox-team or a boat earns for a day's hire, so workers can be hired without haggling.
distinctFrom: corvee_labour is unpaid obligation; hire tariffs set the price of free hired work.

name: Private banking houses
desc: Family firms take deposits, pay on written orders and lend against land, linking farmers, merchants and the treasury.
distinctFrom: interest_bearing_credit is the single loan; banking houses are standing firms holding deposits.

name: Weekly rest day
desc: One day in seven, servants, hired workers and draught animals are released from work by law.
distinctFrom: Working-hours limits in factory_inspection (A8) are enforced by inspectors; this is a customary rest day.

name: Water-turn shares
desc: Those who dig a channel own its flow in timed turns that can be inherited or sold, so new channels are dug.
distinctFrom: water_rights fixes duties on existing canals; water-turn shares make new water a tradable property.

name: Sea loans
desc: Lenders advance money on a ship and cargo, repayable only if the voyage succeeds, so the merchant does not bear the risk of loss alone.
distinctFrom: insurance_underwriting (A7) prices risk separately from credit; the sea loan combines loan and insurance.

name: Public physicians
desc: The city pays a salaried physician to treat its citizens, rich and poor alike.
distinctFrom: public_health_board (A7) holds powers of quarantine; public physicians treat individual patients.

name: Water commissioners
desc: A permanent office maintains the aqueducts, licenses private connections and punishes theft of water.
distinctFrom: building_regulation governs construction; the water commission runs a public supply.

name: Child-support foundations
desc: Endowed funds pay a monthly allowance to poor children in each town, financed by interest on loans to local landowners.
distinctFrom: public_granaries feeds citizens at large; alimenta is targeted at children.

name: Commenda partnership
desc: A stay-at-home investor funds a travelling merchant for one voyage and they split the profit, so a young trader without capital can start out.
distinctFrom: joint_stock pools many investors in a permanent company; the commenda is a two-party contract for one venture.

name: Hospitals
desc: Endowed hospitals with wards, physicians and pharmacies take in the sick without charge.
distinctFrom: public_physicians (A5) are salaried doctors; hospitals are permanent institutions with beds.

name: Stinted commons
desc: The village court limits how many beasts each holding may graze on the common, so the pasture is not overgrazed.
distinctFrom: forest_law reserves woods for a lord; stinting shares a pasture among commoners.

name: Mutual-aid fraternities
desc: Members pay regular dues into a common box that supports them when sick and pays for their burial.
distinctFrom: craft_guilds regulates a trade; fraternities insure their members.

name: Apprenticeship indentures
desc: A written indenture binds a youth to a master for years of training in return for board and the right to become a journeyman.
distinctFrom: craft_guilds governs masters; apprenticeship is the training contract that makes them.

name: Water boards
desc: Landholders elect a board that levies a rate, keeps the dikes and drains the polders.
distinctFrom: water_rights allocates water; water boards are standing bodies that build and keep flood defences.

name: Insurance underwriting
desc: Underwriters take a share of a ship's or a life's risk for a premium priced on recorded losses.
distinctFrom: maritime_loans fold insurance into credit; underwriting sells risk cover on its own.

name: Organised fire-fighting
desc: Towns keep engines, hoses and trained crews ready to answer any fire.
distinctFrom: building_regulation prevents fires by design; brigades fight them when they start.

name: Turnpike trusts
desc: Trusts collect tolls from road users and spend them on resurfacing and straightening the highway.
distinctFrom: customs_tolls raises revenue; turnpike trusts spend road tolls on the road itself.

name: Friendly societies
desc: Wage-earners pay weekly into registered societies that pay benefit in sickness, old age and death.
distinctFrom: mutual_aid_fraternities are guild bodies; friendly societies are open, registered insurance clubs.

name: Social insurance
desc: The law requires workers and employers to pay into funds that cover sickness, accident and old age.
distinctFrom: friendly_societies is voluntary; social insurance is compulsory and state-backed.

name: Municipal waterworks
desc: The city builds and runs its own filtered water supply and sewers for every street.
distinctFrom: sanitary_engineering is the technique; this is the civic duty to supply every street.

name: Compulsory vaccination
desc: The law requires every infant to be vaccinated against smallpox and records each vaccination.
distinctFrom: vaccination is the medical technique; this is the legal duty that makes coverage universal.

name: Labour exchanges
desc: Public offices list vacancies and job-seekers and match them across the country.
distinctFrom: hire_tariffs set wages; labour exchanges match workers to jobs.

name: Workmen's compensation
desc: Employers must compensate workers injured on the job, whoever was at fault.
distinctFrom: factory_inspection prevents accidents; compensation pays for them.

name: Industrial arbitration
desc: Disputes between unions and employers go to a conciliation board or arbitration court instead of a strike.
distinctFrom: labour_unions organises workers; arbitration settles their disputes without a stoppage.

name: Minimum wage
desc: Wage boards set a legal floor under the pay of the lowest-paid trades.
distinctFrom: hire_tariffs fixes customary rates; the minimum wage is a floor, not a fixed price.

name: Commodity exchange
desc: Graded grain and cotton are traded for present and future delivery on a regulated exchange.
distinctFrom: market_fairs meet periodically for goods in hand; the exchange trades graded lots continuously and forward.

name: Housing reform acts
desc: Councils may condemn unfit slums and require new dwellings to meet standards of light, drainage and soundness.
distinctFrom: building_regulation governs height and fire; housing acts set minimum standards of habitability.

name: Deposit insurance
desc: A public fund guarantees ordinary deposits, so savers no longer lose everything when a bank fails.
distinctFrom: central_banking manages the currency; deposit insurance protects the individual saver.

name: Countercyclical demand management
desc: The state cuts taxes and spends in slumps, and restrains demand in booms, to keep output steady.
distinctFrom: central_planning sets output by plan; demand management steers a market economy.

name: Managed exchange rates
desc: Currencies are pegged to an agreed standard and defended by central banks with a shared reserve fund.
distinctFrom: multilateral_trade_rules binds tariffs; this binds the currencies trade is paid in.

name: Farm price support
desc: The state buys surplus grain at a guaranteed price and holds it in reserve stocks.
distinctFrom: public_granaries is a city's famine stock; price support is a national reserve bought to hold up farm prices.

name: Microfinance
desc: Small loans are made to groups of poor borrowers who guarantee each other, without collateral.
distinctFrom: cooperatives share a business; microfinance lends to individuals backed by group guarantee.

name: Special economic zones
desc: Designated districts offer foreign firms low tariffs, light regulation and ready sites, drawing industry and workers.
distinctFrom: customs_union removes tariffs between states; a zone removes them for one district.

name: Collective bargaining law
desc: Employers must recognise a union chosen by their workers and bargain with it in good faith.
distinctFrom: labour_unions makes combination legal; this law obliges employers to bargain.

name: Unemployment insurance
desc: Insured workers who lose their jobs draw a weekly benefit while they look for work.
distinctFrom: social_insurance covers sickness and age; this covers loss of work.

name: Occupational safety agencies
desc: An agency sets exposure limits and safety standards for every workplace, not only factories.
distinctFrom: factory_inspection covers mills and hours; this sets scientific exposure limits across all work.

name: Public vocational training
desc: Schools and employers jointly train young people in trades to a national standard.
distinctFrom: apprenticeship is a private contract with a master; this is a public, certified system.

name: Equal pay law
desc: Employers must pay women the same as men for the same work.
distinctFrom: civil_rights_law bans discrimination broadly; equal pay governs wages for the same work.

name: Guest-worker programmes
desc: States agree to recruit workers abroad on fixed contracts to fill labour shortages.
distinctFrom: refugee_protection admits those fleeing danger; guest-worker schemes recruit labour by contract.

name: Universal social security
desc: Every citizen is covered from cradle to grave: insurance for all and a national safety net beneath it.
distinctFrom: social_insurance covers insured workers; universal social security covers every citizen.

name: School meals
desc: Schools serve every pupil a free or cheap midday meal.
distinctFrom: alimenta pays a cash allowance; school meals feed children directly.

name: Conditional cash transfers
desc: Poor mothers receive monthly cash on condition that children attend school and health checks.
distinctFrom: school_meals feeds pupils; transfers pay families for schooling and health visits.

name: Refugee protection
desc: States may not send refugees back to danger and grant them legal status and relief.
distinctFrom: guest_worker_programmes recruit labour; refugee protection admits people fleeing danger.

name: Universal health care
desc: Medical care is free at the point of use for every resident, paid for from taxes or universal insurance.
distinctFrom: social_insurance covers insured workers; universal care covers every resident.

name: Mass immunization programmes
desc: Health services vaccinate every child against measles, polio, diphtheria and whooping cough on a fixed schedule.
distinctFrom: compulsory_vaccination covers smallpox; this schedules many vaccines for every child.

name: International health regulations
desc: States report outbreaks to a common body and apply agreed, limited quarantine rules at ports and borders.
distinctFrom: public_health_board acts within one polity; these rules coordinate between polities.

name: Drug regulation
desc: New medicines must be proven safe and effective in trials before sale.
distinctFrom: pharmacology compiles remedies; regulation requires proof before sale.

name: Primary health care
desc: Trained village health workers give basic care, clean water advice and maternal care in every community.
distinctFrom: national_health_service is a hospital-based system; primary care puts trained workers in every village.

name: Public housing
desc: Councils build and let standard homes at controlled rents on a large scale.
distinctFrom: housing_acts set standards; public housing builds the homes.

name: National highway programmes
desc: A national authority plans and finances a network of motorways linking every region.
distinctFrom: turnpike_trusts maintain local roads; a national programme builds a planned trunk network.

name: Metropolitan transit authorities
desc: One public authority runs a city's buses, trams and metro as a single network.
distinctFrom: zoning governs land use; the transit authority moves people between zones.

name: Planned new towns
desc: Development corporations build complete new towns, with homes, factories and services, to take people from crowded cities.
distinctFrom: planned_cities lays out one town; new towns are a programme of founding.

name: River basin authorities
desc: One authority manages a whole river basin's dams, locks, flood control and power.
distinctFrom: water_boards keep local dikes; a basin authority plans an entire river.

name: Soil conservation
desc: Advisers and grants teach contour ploughing, terracing and shelter belts to stop soil blowing and washing away.
distinctFrom: nature_conservation sets land aside; soil conservation keeps farmland productive.

name: Fisheries management
desc: Coastal states set catch quotas in their waters to let fish stocks recover.
distinctFrom: stinted_commons caps grazing on land; this caps catches at sea.

name: Public works relief
desc: The state hires the unemployed to build roads, bridges, dams and parks.
distinctFrom: corvee_labour is compulsory; relief work is paid work offered to the unemployed.

name: Wayfinding lore
desc: Bands memorise routes, landmarks, water holes and star rises in song and story, so a party can travel far beyond its home range and find its way back.
distinctFrom: oral_tradition carries any story; this is the practical knowledge of routes used for travel.

name: Guest right
desc: Strangers who come in peace are fed and protected for a time, so people can cross other bands' land to trade, marry or resettle without being treated as raiders.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange moves goods between partners; guest right protects the person travelling.

name: Village defences
desc: The village digs ditches, raises a wall or palisade and keeps a watch, so raiders cannot simply carry off the stored harvest.
distinctFrom: war_band raids others; defences protect the community's own stores.

name: Warrior retinues
desc: A chief keeps armed followers who are fed from his hall and fight at his call, and who also collect what is owed to him.
distinctFrom: war_band forms for one raid; a retinue is kept all year by one leader.

name: Daughter villages
desc: When a village grows too large, a group of households leaves with seed and stock to found a new village nearby.
distinctFrom: daughter_colonies (A4) are overseas cities; this is overland village fission among farmers.

name: Island colonization voyages
desc: Settlers sail to islands with seed, breeding stock and supplies to found new communities beyond sight of land.
distinctFrom: wayfinding_lore is route memory on land; this is planned settlement across open water.

name: Exchange partners
desc: Communities keep standing exchange partners in other villages and renew the tie at feasts, so axes, shell and stone pass from hand to hand across hundreds of km.
distinctFrom: gift_exchange is one-off giving; partnerships are lasting ties between communities.

name: Campaign supply depots
desc: Officials stock grain, fodder and weapons at stations along the march so an army can campaign far from home.
distinctFrom: service_tenure raises soldiers; this feeds them on the march.

name: Royal expeditions
desc: The crown sends organised expeditions to distant lands for incense, gold and stone, and records what they find.
distinctFrom: royal_envoys go to known courts; expeditions go to lands not yet known.

name: Frontier fortresses
desc: A chain of forts with commandants and scribes holds a frontier, controls crossings and reports movements to the capital.
distinctFrom: service_tenure settles soldiers on land; fortresses are state garrisons at the border.

name: Siege and road engineers
desc: Specialist troops build ramps, bridges and tracks for the army, and their skills are turned to roads in peace.
distinctFrom: siege_ram is the machine; this is the corps that builds and moves armies.

name: State resettlement
desc: The state moves whole communities from conquered lands to new provinces to farm empty land and break old loyalties.
distinctFrom: daughter_colonies send volunteers out; resettlement moves whole communities by order.

name: Veteran colonies
desc: Discharged soldiers receive surveyed plots in new or conquered land, founding colonies loyal to the state.
distinctFrom: daughter_colonies are civic foundations; these are state grants to discharged soldiers.

name: Military roads
desc: The state builds straight, paved, all-weather roads to move armies fast; merchants and couriers use them too.
distinctFrom: road_paved is the technique; this is the state road network and its upkeep.

name: Hegemonic leagues
desc: Allied cities swear to a common league led by the strongest, paying into a shared treasury for a common fleet or army.
distinctFrom: oath_alliance binds equals; a league has a leader, a treasury and assessed dues.

name: Military treatises
desc: Commanders write down doctrine on scouting, spies, supply and terrain, and officers study it.
distinctFrom: military_academies (A7) are schools; this is written doctrine itself.

name: Slave-soldier corps
desc: The ruler buys or levies boys from outside, trains them as soldiers, and promotes the able to command and governorships.
distinctFrom: military_rule is a regime; this is a recruitment and promotion system.

name: Safe-conduct
desc: A ruler's written guarantee protects named foreigners, their goods and their servants while they travel in his land.
distinctFrom: guest_right is custom among bands; safe-conduct is a written state guarantee.

name: Merchant consuls
desc: Merchants abroad elect or receive a consul who judges their disputes, speaks for them to the ruler and keeps their warehouse.
distinctFrom: trade_treaties are agreements; consuls are officers resident abroad who enforce them.

name: Settlement charters
desc: Lords grant written charters with free plots, low dues and self-government to attract settlers to frontier land.
distinctFrom: municipal_charter governs a town; settlement charters recruit settlers to empty land.

name: Marcher lordships
desc: Frontier districts are granted to lords with wide powers to raise troops, build castles and push the border outward.
distinctFrom: frontier_fortresses are royal garrisons; marches delegate the frontier to lords.

name: Army magazines
desc: The state keeps grain magazines for the army along the frontier and opens them to the public in famine years.
distinctFrom: public_granaries are civil stores; magazines are military stores also used in famine.

name: Corps of engineers
desc: A permanent corps of trained engineers designs fortresses, bridges and roads and surveys the ground.
distinctFrom: siege_engineers are field troops; this is a trained professional corps.

name: Chartered companies
desc: The state charters a company with a trade monopoly and powers to fortify, make treaties and govern overseas.
distinctFrom: joint_stock is the firm form; this is a firm granted sovereign powers overseas.

name: Military railways
desc: The staff plans railway timetables to move troops and supplies, and lines are built where the army needs them.
distinctFrom: railway is the technology; this is its planned military use.

name: Trained reserves
desc: Conscripts serve a short term, then return home as trained reserves called up only in war.
distinctFrom: universal_conscription calls men up; reserves send them home trained.

name: Colonial regiments
desc: The colonial government raises regiments from local recruits under contract to garrison and police its territories.
distinctFrom: mercenary_contracts hire foreign soldiers; these are standing colonial units.

name: Consular service
desc: Salaried state consuls in foreign ports protect nationals and report on markets, prices and shipping.
distinctFrom: merchant_consuls serve one merchant community; this is a state service reporting on markets.

name: River commissions
desc: States along a river set common rules, tolls and channel works under a standing commission so ships move freely.
distinctFrom: international_organizations are general bodies; this regulates one shared river.

name: Coaling stations
prereq: state_navy AND (steamboat OR screw_propeller) AND colonial_administration
desc: The navy holds a chain of ports stocked with coal so steam ships can cross oceans.
distinctFrom: state_navy is the fleet; this is its global base network.

name: Geographical societies
desc: Learned societies fund expeditions, publish maps and train explorers in survey.
distinctFrom: state_exploration is crown voyages; this is private learned exploration.

name: Assisted emigration
desc: Colonies pay the passage of chosen emigrants from land-sale revenue so labourers can reach distant colonies.
distinctFrom: settler_land_grants give land; this pays for the journey.

name: Colonial self-government
desc: Settler colonies gain their own cabinet answerable to an elected assembly, while foreign affairs stay with the empire.
distinctFrom: indirect_rule governs through princes; this hands self-government to settlers.

name: Peacekeeping
desc: International forces, accepted by both sides, watch ceasefire lines and protect aid convoys.
distinctFrom: collective_security pledges action; peacekeeping is a neutral force in the field.

name: International food aid
desc: Surplus food is shipped through international programmes to countries in famine.
distinctFrom: public_granaries are national; this pools food across states.

name: Law of the sea
desc: Treaties fix territorial waters and economic zones, giving coastal states rights over fisheries and the seabed.
distinctFrom: law_of_nations covers neutrality at sea; this assigns ocean resources.

name: Civil aviation agreements
desc: States agree rights to fly over and land in each other's territory and common air safety rules.
distinctFrom: international_organizations is general; this opens airspace.

name: Development lending
desc: International banks lend to governments for roads, dams and power plants.
distinctFrom: central_banking is national; this lends across borders for infrastructure.

name: Passport-free travel areas
desc: Member states abolish passport checks at their common borders and let citizens live and work across them.
distinctFrom: customs_union frees goods; this frees people.

name: Academic exchange
desc: Governments fund students and scholars to study and teach abroad.
distinctFrom: research_university is domestic; this links universities across states.

name: International standards bodies
desc: States and industries agree common standards for parts, measures and shipping containers.
distinctFrom: multilateral_trade_rules govern tariffs; standards govern the goods themselves.

name: Shared-river treaties
desc: States sharing a river divide its water by treaty so irrigation works on both sides have an assured supply.
distinctFrom: river_commissions regulate navigation; this allocates water.

name: International weather service
desc: States share weather observations in real time so every country can forecast storms, frost and drought.
distinctFrom: weather_prediction is the science; this is the exchange of observations.

name: Intelligence agencies
desc: A permanent agency gathers and analyses intelligence from agents, signals and photographs.
distinctFrom: general_staff plans; this agency collects information.

name: Satellite reconnaissance
desc: Satellites photograph any part of the earth and return the images.
distinctFrom: military_intelligence uses agents and signals; this uses orbital imagery.

name: Motor transport corps
desc: Army lorry columns carry supplies far beyond the railhead.
distinctFrom: military_railways move by rail; this carries supplies by road from the railhead.

name: Civil defence
desc: Wardens, shelters and emergency food depots protect civilians in war and disaster.
distinctFrom: total_mobilization directs production; civil defence protects civilians.

name: Ration books
desc: Scarce food is shared by fixed rations per person so households get through shortages.
distinctFrom: total_mobilization directs production; rationing divides consumption.

name: Veterans' benefits
desc: Former soldiers receive paid schooling, training and home loans.
distinctFrom: universal_conscription calls up; this rewards and retrains after service.

name: Counter-insurgency doctrine
desc: Armies and police protect the population, gather intelligence and address grievances to isolate insurgents.
distinctFrom: civil_police keep ordinary order; this counters armed insurgency.

name: Strategic stockpiles
desc: The state stores fuel, metals and food and releases them to the market when supplies fail.
distinctFrom: civil_defence stocks food locally; this holds national strategic reserves.

name: All-volunteer forces
desc: The state ends conscription and recruits paid professionals.
distinctFrom: mercenary_contracts hire foreigners; this recruits citizens as paid volunteers.

name: Defence research agencies
desc: Defence agencies fund research at universities and laboratories.
distinctFrom: science_policy funds civil science; this funds military research.

name: Independent air force
desc: Air power is organised as its own service, which flies reconnaissance and survey.
distinctFrom: aircraft is the machine; this is the service.

name: Polar research stations
desc: States keep permanent scientific stations in the polar regions and share their findings.
distinctFrom: geographical_societies fund expeditions; this keeps permanent shared stations.

name: Commonwealth association
desc: Former colonies and the old imperial power form a free association of equal states.
distinctFrom: decolonization ends empire; this keeps a voluntary association.

name: Frontier development programmes
desc: The state plans and funds settlement of thinly peopled interior land, with new towns, roads and farms.
distinctFrom: settler_land_grants offer land; this plans and funds the whole settlement.

name: Overseas departments
desc: Former colonies become full parts of the state, with the same laws and representation.
distinctFrom: decolonization separates; this integrates.

name: States reorganisation
desc: A new state redraws its internal provinces along language lines.
distinctFrom: federal_republic sets the units; this redraws them.

name: Indigenous land rights
desc: Law recognises indigenous peoples' title to their land and returns some of it.
distinctFrom: decolonization frees colonies; this restores rights inside settler states.

name: Ritual music and dance
desc: Bands sing, drum and dance together at night and at gatherings. Shared rhythm binds people who quarrel by day.
distinctFrom: oral_tradition is remembered lore; ritual music is a group practice of sound and movement.

name: Landscape lore
desc: Bands memorize a wide landscape as a chain of named landmarks, water holes and seasonal resources, and teach it to the young.
distinctFrom: C3's seasonal_round is a yearly schedule of known camps; landscape lore is the remembered map that lets a band go beyond them.

name: Calendar keepers
desc: Ritual specialists watch the moon and sunrise points and announce when to sow, harvest and hold the festivals.
distinctFrom: calendar_lunar is the technique of counting months; calendar keepers are the office that turns it into a farming timetable.

name: Herd lore
desc: Herders keep the lineage, temper and grazing of each animal in memory and pass on when to cull, breed and move the flock.
distinctFrom: sheep_goat is domestication itself; herd lore is the remembered management practice built on it.

name: House painting and plaster
desc: Households replaster and paint their walls each year with hunting scenes and patterns, and rebuild ancestral houses on the same spot.
distinctFrom: C1's megalithic_monuments are communal stone enclosures; this is the decoration and upkeep of ordinary houses.

name: Sign systems
desc: Communities use a repertoire of incised signs on pots, spindle whorls and figurines to mark owners, offerings and messages.
distinctFrom: C2's storehouse_sealing is impressed seals on stores; sign systems are a shared repertoire of written marks before full writing.

name: Epic literature
desc: Heroic tales once sung are written down, copied in the schools and recited at court and festival.
distinctFrom: oral_tradition is unwritten lore; epic literature is a fixed written canon taught and recited.

name: Lexical lists
desc: Scribes copy standard lists of words for trades, goods, animals and places, the first ordered body of knowledge.
distinctFrom: scribal_schools is the school; lexical lists are the standard reference corpus it copies.

name: Victory stelae
desc: Kings set up carved and inscribed stones at frontiers and city gates announcing their victories and warning rebels.
distinctFrom: C2's published_law displays laws for citizens; victory stelae proclaim a ruler's might to subjects and enemies.

name: Palace library
desc: The palace collects and catalogues copies of scholarly, religious and medical texts from across the realm.
distinctFrom: royal_archives keeps administrative records; the library collects scholarly works.

name: Letter schools
desc: Fee-paying teachers teach citizens' children reading, writing and music in small schools.
distinctFrom: scribal_schools train a professional caste; letter schools teach ordinary citizens' children.

name: Agronomic treatises
prereq: scribal_schools AND (alphabet_vowels OR chinese_script OR abjad)
desc: Landowners write and read manuals on crops, soils, manuring and estate management.
distinctFrom: iron_mouldboard and other techs are tools; treatises are the written learning of how to farm.

name: Medical schools
desc: Physicians train pupils in schools with a shared corpus of texts, case records and dissection.
distinctFrom: C3's public_physicians is a city paying a doctor; medical schools train doctors.

name: Rhetoric schools
desc: Paid teachers train young men to argue in courts and assemblies, the path to a public career.
distinctFrom: philosophical_schools pursue truth; rhetoric schools train advocates and politicians.

name: Cathedral and madrasa schools
desc: Endowed schools at cathedrals and mosques teach grammar, law and theology to boys who will become clergy, judges and clerks.
distinctFrom: scribal_schools train scribes for a palace; these endowed schools train clergy and jurists across a whole faith.

name: Chartered universities
desc: Masters and students form self-governing corporations with charters, faculties and degrees recognized across realms.
distinctFrom: state_academy is a ruler's school; a chartered university is a self-governing corporation granting degrees.

name: Patronage of translation
desc: Patrons pay scholars to translate the science and philosophy of other languages and copy the translations widely.
distinctFrom: humanism recovers one's own classics; this imports another civilization's learning. The runtime entity inst.translation_movement (institution, not live) is the house of translation; this civic is the patronage that funds it.

name: Printed classics
desc: The state prints authorized editions of the classics and sells them cheaply to schools and examination candidates.
distinctFrom: woodblock_print is the technique; printed classics is the state publishing programme.

name: Vernacular literature
desc: Poets and storytellers write in the spoken tongue for lay readers rather than in the learned language.
distinctFrom: epic_literature is a learned canon in a classical tongue; vernacular literature writes in the people's speech.

name: Geographic compendia
desc: Scholars compile travellers' and merchants' reports into world descriptions with maps and itineraries.
distinctFrom: cartography is map-making; compendia gather what is known of the world into reference works.

name: Printed newspapers
desc: Printers issue weekly sheets of news and merchants' price currents gathered from the posts.
distinctFrom: state_gazette is official decrees; newspapers are commercial news sold to the public.

name: Humanist colleges
desc: Colleges teach graded classes of boys Latin, Greek, rhetoric and history from printed textbooks.
distinctFrom: humanism is the scholarly movement; humanist colleges are the schools that spread it to boys.

name: Language academies
desc: Chartered academies fix the standard language in an official dictionary and grammar.
distinctFrom: humanism studies classical Latin; language academies standardize the national vernacular.

name: Telegraph news agencies
desc: Agencies gather news and market prices by telegraph and sell them to every paper at once.
distinctFrom: mass_press sells papers; the agencies supply wired news and prices to all papers.

name: Advertising
desc: Agencies buy space in the papers and write notices that tell buyers what is for sale, where and at what price.
distinctFrom: telegraph_news_agencies carry news to the press; advertising carries sellers' offers to readers.

name: Public libraries
desc: Towns fund free lending libraries and reading rooms open to every resident.
distinctFrom: palace_library serves the court's scholars; public libraries lend to everyone.

name: Mining and technical academies
desc: State academies train engineers and mine officials in chemistry, mechanics and geology.
distinctFrom: research_university pursues research; technical academies train practising engineers.

name: Normal schools
desc: Teacher-training colleges prepare elementary teachers in subject and method to a common standard.
distinctFrom: compulsory_education requires attendance; normal schools supply the teachers.

name: Agricultural colleges
desc: Colleges teach scientific farming, run experimental fields and train estate managers and farmers' sons.
distinctFrom: C2's agricultural_extension sends agents to farms; colleges train the agents and farmers.

name: Medical education reform
desc: Medical schools are tied to universities and teaching hospitals, with laboratory science and clinical training required.
distinctFrom: medical_schools pass on a tradition; this reform ties training to research science and hospitals.

name: Women's higher education
desc: Colleges and secondary schools open to women and girls, and women begin to take degrees and enter the professions.
distinctFrom: normal_schools train teachers; this opens all higher study to women.

name: Industrial exhibitions
desc: Great halls display the newest machines, crops and manufactures to millions of visitors and juries award prizes.
distinctFrom: public_museums display the past; exhibitions display the newest products for adoption.

name: National literature
desc: Scholars collect folk tales and songs and print them as the nation's own literature, taught in schools.
distinctFrom: vernacular_literature is authored works; national literature collects folk tradition as a nation's heritage.

name: Broadcast market reports
desc: Daily radio bulletins read out crop and livestock prices so farmers know where and when to sell.
distinctFrom: telegraph agencies serve the press; broadcast reports reach the farmer directly.

name: Famine early warning
desc: Agencies combine satellite crop monitoring with market and household reports and publish warnings months before a famine.
distinctFrom: C2's disaster_management organizes response; early warning is the published forecast that triggers it.

name: Public opinion polling
desc: Pollsters question a sample of the public and publish what people think of leaders and policies.
distinctFrom: C2's sample_surveys measure crops and jobs; polling measures opinion.

name: Universal telephone service
desc: Telephone carriers must connect every household and farm at regulated rates, cross-subsidizing remote lines.
distinctFrom: public_postal_service carries letters; this obliges telephone carriers to serve everyone.

name: Social media
desc: Anyone can publish posts, photos and video to followers worldwide on shared platforms.
distinctFrom: internet_governance sets rules for the network; social media is mass publishing on it.

name: Satellite communications consortium
desc: An international consortium runs satellites that carry telephone and television between continents.
distinctFrom: universal_telephone_service is a domestic mandate; this is the international network.

name: Civil satellite navigation
desc: Governments open military navigation satellites to free civilian use worldwide.
distinctFrom: gps is the technology; this is the policy of free civil access.

name: Script and language reform
desc: The state replaces or simplifies the national script and standard language to speed up mass literacy.
distinctFrom: language_academies codify an elite standard; script reform changes how the whole population writes.

name: National laboratories
desc: The state builds large laboratories with permanent staff and giant instruments beyond any university's means.
distinctFrom: science_policy funds research by grants; national labs are state-run research institutions.

name: Think tanks
desc: Independent institutes employ researchers to analyse public policy and propose reforms to governments and parties.
distinctFrom: political_philosophy is reflection on rule; think tanks are paid policy research institutes.

name: National accounts
desc: Statisticians measure the whole economy's output, income and spending in one system of accounts each year.
distinctFrom: official_statistics counts people; national accounts measure the economy.

name: Agricultural research system
desc: National and international stations breed high-yield crop varieties and test them across climates.
distinctFrom: C2's agricultural_extension teaches farmers; this system breeds and tests the varieties.

name: Open access science
desc: Research papers and data are published free online for anyone to read and reuse.
distinctFrom: scientific_societies publish proceedings to members; open access publishes free to all.

name: Clinical trials
desc: Treatments are tested by randomized controlled trials before they are adopted.
distinctFrom: medical_education_reform trains doctors; clinical trials test what they prescribe.

name: Operations research
desc: Scientists apply mathematics to routing, scheduling and supply problems of armies and firms.
distinctFrom: national_accounts measure the economy; operations research optimizes its logistics.

name: Civil space agency
desc: A civilian agency runs space science, mapping and exploration programmes.
distinctFrom: national_laboratories pursue physics; the space agency runs exploration and earth survey.

name: Mass literacy campaigns
desc: The state mobilizes teachers and students to teach every adult to read within a few years.
distinctFrom: compulsory_education schools children; literacy campaigns teach the adults left out.

name: Universal secondary education
desc: Every child stays at school into the teens, in free state secondary schools.
distinctFrom: humanist_colleges served an elite; universal secondary education enrols every child.

name: Mass higher education
desc: Public grants and new campuses open university study to a large share of each generation.
distinctFrom: research_university is a model of research; mass higher education is enrolment at scale.

name: Distance education
desc: Adults study for degrees at home through broadcast lectures, post and later the internet.
distinctFrom: mass_higher_education builds campuses; distance education reaches those who cannot attend.

name: International student exchange
desc: Governments fund students and scholars to study abroad and recognize each other's degrees.
distinctFrom: cultural_institutes teach a language abroad; exchanges send students to study abroad.

name: Film industry
desc: Studios make feature films shown in thousands of cinemas to mass weekly audiences.
distinctFrom: public_theatre is live drama; film is mass-reproduced drama shown everywhere at once.

name: Arts councils
desc: Public bodies grant tax money at arm's length to theatres, orchestras, galleries and artists.
distinctFrom: court_patronage is a ruler's taste; arts councils are arm's-length public funding.

name: Cultural institutes
desc: States fund institutes abroad that teach their language and present their culture.
distinctFrom: international_student_exchange sends students; institutes teach the language abroad.

name: Recorded music industry
desc: Firms record and sell music to every home and radio station, making popular music a mass culture.
distinctFrom: public_opera is live performance; recorded music is mass-reproduced sound.

name: Modernist design
desc: Designers and architects plan compact, standardized dwellings and furniture for mass housing.
distinctFrom: arts_academies train artists; modernist design applies art to mass housing and goods.

name: Public art programmes
desc: The state employs artists to paint murals and make public works that teach history to all citizens.
distinctFrom: arts_councils make grants at arm's length; public art programmes commission and employ artists directly.

name: Purpose-built granaries
desc: Raised floors, sealed pits and mud-plastered bins keep stored grain dry and free of pests, so a harvest lasts until the next one and beyond.
distinctFrom: cereal_domesticated changes the plant; this changes how its grain is kept. The granary building has no research requirement; this node improves what granaries hold and how little rots.

name: Iron farm tools
