desc: Forged iron sickles, hoe blades and ploughshares hold an edge and outlast stone and bronze, letting farmers clear forest and work harder soils.
distinctFrom: iron_bloomery makes the metal; this puts it into everyday farm tools. Unlike heavy_plough it is a hand-tool and share capability, not a new plough.

name: Three-field rotation
desc: Fields rotate through winter grain, spring legumes or oats, and fallow, so only a third lies idle; oats feed horses and pulses restore the soil.
distinctFrom: crop_rotation_norfolk abolishes fallow with fodder roots and clover; this is the earlier regime that halves fallow and adds a spring course.

name: Herring buss and sea-curing
desc: Decked fishing ships stay out for weeks with drift nets, gutting and salting the herring aboard, so the catch reaches distant markets.
distinctFrom: fishing_hook is subsistence line fishing; this is an offshore commercial fishery with preservation at sea.

name: Tinplate
desc: Thin iron sheet coated with molten tin so it will not rust: light, cheap, sealable boxes, canisters and kitchenware, and later the tin can.
distinctFrom: sheet_metal is hammered bronze for vessels and armour; tinplate is rust-proofed iron sheet for sealed containers (the missing bridge to canning).

name: Crucible cast steel
desc: Blister steel melted in sealed clay crucibles and cast into ingots: uniform, slag-free tool steel for files, springs, razors and edge tools.
distinctFrom: wootz is small-batch South Indian crucible steel for blades without coke; this is coke-fired, homogeneous cast tool steel made in quantity for machine and edge tools.

name: Galvanized corrugated iron
desc: Iron sheet dipped in molten zinc and rolled into corrugations: a light, stiff, rust-resistant roof and wall cladding shipped flat and nailed up anywhere.
distinctFrom: portland_cement replaces timber in walls and foundations; galvanized iron replaces shingle and thatch roofing that must be renewed, chiefly cutting upkeep.

name: Masonry dam and reservoir
desc: Walls of stone and earth across a valley hold back seasonal runoff, so channels can water the fields through a dry year.
distinctFrom: irrigation_canal leads water already flowing; this stores it across seasons. hydroelectric (A9) is a power dam, not water storage for farming.

name: Multi-storey apartment block
desc: Brick-faced concrete walls carry several floors of rented flats over street shops, packing many households onto one plot.
distinctFrom: timber_frame houses one large household under one roof; this stacks many households vertically. The civic building_regulation (A5) regulates such blocks; this is the building technique itself.

name: Balloon framing
desc: Light sawn studs nailed together replace heavy jointed timbers, so a small crew can raise a house in days.
distinctFrom: timber_frame is jointed post-and-beam; this is a nailed frame of light sawn studs with no joinery, which cuts the labour per dwelling.

name: Industrialised panel building
desc: Wall and floor panels are cast in factories and lifted into place by crane, so whole housing estates rise with little site labour.
distinctFrom: reinforced_concrete is the material, poured on site; skyscraper is height and density. This is factory prefabrication of whole dwellings, which cuts labour per dwelling.

name: Lifting crane
desc: A timber jib with pulleys and a winch lifts heavy blocks and beams: small gangs raise walls and roofs that once needed ramps and crowds.
distinctFrom: mechanics_archimedean (A5) is the theory of the lever and compound pulley; the crane is the practical builder's machine, about 250 years earlier.

name: Coal as fuel
desc: Mining and burning mineral coal for heating, lime-burning, forging and smelting, where firewood has grown scarce.
distinctFrom: coke (A7) is coal carbonised for blast furnaces; this node is the earlier use of raw coal as a fuel. charcoal (A2) is a wood fuel.

name: Mine pumping engines
desc: Water wheels and horse gins drive chains of pumps and lifting rods that keep deep mine shafts dry.
distinctFrom: steam_atmospheric (A7, 1712) drains mines with a heat engine; this node is the water- and animal-powered pumping it replaced.

name: Coal-gas lighting
desc: Coal is baked in retorts and the gas piped under the streets to burners: lit streets, mills, homes, and later fuel for gas engines.
distinctFrom: electric_light (A8, 1879) is electric incandescence; this is the earlier piped coal-gas supply, also the fuel of gas_engine.

name: Desert caravan
desc: Strings of camels, with wells, guides and halting places, carry goods across deserts that no cart or donkey could cross, so towns far apart can trade overland.
distinctFrom: trade (A3) is exchange between settlements within ordinary route range by any carrier; this is the specific ability to cross waterless country, lengthening the longest viable overland route rather than cheapening haulage.

name: Sprung coach and stage service
desc: Coaches hung on straps and later steel springs, drawn by fresh teams changed at regular stages, carry passengers, mail and light goods on timetabled runs between towns.
distinctFrom: horseshoe (A6) protects the animal and macadam (A8) improves the surface; this is the vehicle and staging system, the only A7 overland transport node (the A7 transport lane is otherwise empty).

name: Logarithms
desc: Tables that turn multiplication into addition. Navigators, astronomers and surveyors compute in minutes what took hours, and Gunter's scale puts the method in a ship's master's hands.
distinctFrom: calculus (A7) is the theory of rates; logarithms are a computational shortcut 60 years earlier, used by practitioners rather than theorists.

name: Electrostatics and the lightning rod
desc: Friction machines, the Leyden jar and Franklin's experiments show that lightning is electricity. Grounded rods protect roofs, steeples and powder magazines.
distinctFrom: electromagnetism (A8) is current electricity and induction; electrostatics is the earlier science of charge, and its only direct product is the lightning rod.

name: Synoptic meteorology
desc: Simultaneous barometer readings, telegraphed to one office, become a weather map. Storm warnings reach ports, and frost warnings reach growers.
distinctFrom: weather_prediction (A9, engineering) is computer-based numerical forecasting from 1950; this is the earlier telegraph-and-map forecast, and it bridges barometer_vacuum to it.

name: Metric system
desc: Decimal units defined by nature and kept by international standards. Goods, land and loads are measured the same way in every market.
distinctFrom: standard_weights (A3) are local state standards; the metric system is a decimal, nature-based, international system tied to geodesy and chemistry.

name: Parchment codex
desc: Pages of durable parchment bound between boards. A codex can be opened at any page, indexed and carried, so reference books, law codes and scripture survive and can be consulted quickly.
distinctFrom: papyrus (A3) is the scroll writing surface and paper (A5) the cheap sheet material; this is the bound, page-addressable, long-lasting book format, so its effect is on accumulated knowledge, not on administrative scale.

name: Sustained-yield forestry
desc: Forests divided into measured plots, cut in rotation and replanted so that no more wood is taken each year than grows back. Timber and fuel stop running out.
distinctFrom: forest_law (A6 civic) reserves forests by decree; this is the technical practice of rotation, measurement and replanting that raises the sustained timber harvest. It is the environment lane's first finite node.

name: Steam-powered printing press
desc: Cylinder and then rotary presses driven by steam print thousands of sheets an hour. Daily newspapers sell for a penny, and politics, prices and news reach every reader.
distinctFrom: printing_press (A7) is the hand press of books and pamphlets; this is the mechanised mass-circulation press behind the penny press (mass_press civic). It has no live building of its own, only the civic-discourse effect.

name: Herbal remedies
desc: Knowledge of plants that ease pain, purge worms and dress wounds, passed from healer to healer. The root of every later pharmacopoeia.
distinctFrom: pharmacology (A5) is a written, systematic catalogue; herbal remedies are oral lore, 45,000 years earlier, and the root medicine_recorded writes down.

name: Signal beacons
desc: Chains of watch posts on high ground pass a pre-arranged fire or smoke signal from hilltop to hilltop: news of raiders reaches the capital in hours instead of days.
distinctFrom: optical_telegraph (A7) sends arbitrary coded messages along a line; beacons carry one pre-agreed signal, 3,500 years earlier, for frontier warning.

name: Antiscorbutics
desc: Citrus juice and fresh food prevent scurvy, which killed more sailors on long voyages than storms or battle. Crews and emigrants arrive alive.
distinctFrom: inoculation (A7) protects against one infection; antiscorbutics prevent a deficiency disease of long voyages, with a migration and exploration effect, not mortality.

name: Quinine
desc: The alkaloid of cinchona bark, isolated and dosed, prevents and treats malaria. Settlers and soldiers survive in malarial lands that had killed most newcomers.
distinctFrom: pharmacology (A5) catalogues drugs; quinine is one purified, dosed alkaloid against the deadliest endemic disease, with a colonization effect.

name: Aerial reconnaissance
desc: Aircraft with cameras photograph the land beyond the front and far from home. Maps of unseen country are made from the air.
distinctFrom: radar (A9) detects by radio at night and in cloud for air defence; aerial reconnaissance photographs terrain by daylight, decades earlier, and maps land rather than tracking targets.
